cpu_method.order: Alternating before/after and after/before, one warmup per endpoint. Quiet cohorts; all other validation stopped. No extra timing rounds.
cpu_method.measurement: Fresh CLI child user+system CPU from wait4, wall and minor faults; includes process startup, own-format load, source read, full compilation and detached output retention.
cpu_method.limits: Single short-job cohort per document; sample ranges overlap. Modest paired trends do not establish a robust CPU speedup or TeX-wide claim. Native is a correctness oracle here, not a timed performance endpoint. No prepared replay speed claim.

instructions.method: Separate single whole-job Callgrind run per endpoint/document, CPU3, collect-jumps=yes, default release. Ir counts executed instructions, not CPU time; inclusive function costs overlap.

assembly.method: Separate bounded Conversion::run disassembly from the exact saved default-release binaries. Before Again path copies the active frame and enters Buffer::push; after Again returns directly to local dispatch. Child/Replace pushes remain.
assembly.limits: Compiler function body grows by 1,271 bytes and stack frame by 32 bytes; dynamic instruction work still falls. No assembly-specific tuning performed.

ownership: The active local Task owns its forests; suspended tasks remain on the same stack. Interruption checks occur once before every semantic step, including after Again. Active task is released before existing result/parent cleanup. An Again push previously reused the popped slot and could not grow storage; all potentially growing initial/child pushes remain unchanged.
conclusion: Keep the small general dataflow simplification: exact output/replay and ownership checks pass; whole-job instruction work falls on both documents. CPU changes are modest and separately limited.
